Summary

A quadratic function can be written in the form f​ (x) 5 ax2 1 bx 1 c​, where
a, b, and c are real numbers and a is not equal to zero; therefore, the equation ​
y 5 x2​is an example of a quadratic function. A quadratic function has neither a
constant difference nor a constant ratio between consecutive terms.
